To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) a cDNA, PRF5 (accession number L 35284), was isolated from ripe peach fruit that encoded a protein with a predicted molecular mass of 42,000 D and that was homologous to other endopolygalacturonaes and (b) the expression of PRF5-related RNA was correlated with fruit softening and ripening in a melting cultivar but not in a nonmelting cultivary.
the expression of a polygalacturonate lyase gene in ripe peach fruit correlates with softening and that the expression of this gene differs between cultivars that have different degrees of softness.

(i) the PRF5 cDNA codes for the peach polygalactutronase, (ii) the mRNA levels of PRF5 increase during ripening, (iii) the mRNA levels for PRF5 increase at the melting stage of fruit softening, and (iv) the mRNA levels are higher in melting cultivars than in nonmelting cultivars.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and characterization of a peach polygalecturonase (PG) cDNA and mRNA.
the identification of the gene encoding the endopolygalactouronase in ripe peach fruit.
the molecular biology of the softening process in peach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the peach polygalacturnose gene family consists of a minimum of four genes.

PRF5 is a cDNA for a ripening-related peach endopolygalacturnase, that it is expressed in a cultivar-specific manner, and that it may be a candidate gene involved in the melting stage of softening of peach fruit.
the peach polygalactuonase cDNA, PRF3, was isolated, sequenced, and characterized.

the PRF5 cDNA encodes a peach endopolygalacturanse, that the PRF3 probe detects an endopolygalacturansase-related RNA transcript that increases in ripening fruit, that the PRP3 probe detects two distinct RNA transcripts in ripening peach fruit, that the increase in the 1.7- kb RNA transcript coincides with the melting stage of softening, and that the 1.45- kb transcript may represent a different endopolygalact
PRF3 is a peach gene that is not expressed during ripening in the nonmelting Carolyn peach and is expressed at very low levels in ripe fruit of Fragar.
the PRF3 cDNA is specific for the endopolygalacturonoase of ripe fruit, but that the PRF1 and the PRF3-related sequences are not specific for polygalacturonose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PRF5 cDNA is the first to be cloned from a peach fruit.
the PRF5 cDNA is the first endopolygalacturanse cDNA to be isolated from peach fruit.
the expression of PRF3, and hence of the PRF5 endopolygalacturonaes, is tightly linked to the melting softening stage of ripening.
